groups.reason: The operator-facing capability already exists through the canonical Headless control plane or standard Headless configuration; exposing the desktop IPC command would duplicate that surface. Every command in this group names the covering surface in commandReasons — a claim with no named cover is not a disposition, it is a guess.

commandReasons.companion_create_worker_enrollment: Covered by the `fleet_worker_enrollment_create` RPC arm (companion_api/rpc/diagnostics.rs:110), which mints the same enrollment through security_store::create_worker_enrollment with the same 10-minute TTL. The Tauri variant additionally derives baseUrl and TLS fingerprint from local tunnel/LAN state; a remote caller already knows how it reached the host and supplies those itself.
commandReasons.companion_list_workers: Covered by `fleet_worker_list` (companion_api/rpc/diagnostics.rs:138) — the same list_worker_devices + worker_device_summaries pair, plus an owner check the Tauri arm does not perform. The renderer already treats them as one capability with two bindings (lib/fleet/execution-workers.ts:47).
commandReasons.companion_set_worker: Covered by `fleet_worker_set` (companion_api/rpc/diagnostics.rs:153) and by PUT /api/devices/{device_id}/capabilities (companion_api/api.rs:309); all three funnel into replace_device_capabilities with the identical agent.worker retain/push sequence.
commandReasons.workflow_waitpoint_list_pending: Covered by `workflow_approval_list` (companion_api/rpc/data_sync.rs:448), which calls the same mirror.list_pending_waitpoints() on both the Tauri and Headless dispatch hosts. Coverage is of the operator-facing subset: the remote arm filters to kind approval|risk_gate (data_sync.rs:461), so the machine-consumed `event_wait` kind is not listed remotely — deliberately, since no operator decides one.
commandReasons.workflow_waitpoint_decide: Covered by `workflow_approval_respond` (companion_api/rpc/data_sync.rs:478), which builds the same WorkflowWaitpointDecisionInput and calls the same mirror.decide_waitpoint(). The remote arm accepts approved|rejected only; the timed_out and cancelled outcomes this command also carries are emitted by the runtime, never chosen by an operator.
commandReasons.companion_list_device_grants: Covered by GET /api/devices (companion_api/api.rs:287), which returns the same list_devices() rows this command projects — it differs only by folding each device's capability set into a control/agent_control/terminal boolean triple and by reading the hardcoded local tenant instead of the authenticated one. Same relationship as companion_list_workers to fleet_worker_list.

groups.reason: Subscription account management reads and writes the provider credential vault. It is deliberately desktop-only and is NOT reachable from a remote or mobile client; the desktop UI calls the #[tauri::command] functions directly through transport-tauri, never through companion dispatch. The rationale is written at src-tauri/src/companion_api/rpc/chat.rs:286-292. These were previously filed as covered-by-headless, which asserted the opposite: that the capability was already available remotely.

Operates on the desktop app's own on-disk sqlite-vec store at <app_data>/cognia/vectors.sqlite. HeadlessServices has no vector-store field and no companion RPC arm mentions vector_, so a Headless process neither owns nor can reach that file; the credential pair (vector_save_credentials / vector_delete_credentials) additionally writes the secret store. The cloud-backed half of this family stays covered-by-headless, which is the distinction the single previous group elided.
Renderer or runtime bridge acknowledgement/response plumbing; it is not an operator action and remains behind the internal runtime protocol.

commandReasons.claude_plugin_hook_response: The renderer's answer to a hook the sidecar is blocked on. It is one half of an in-flight call, not an action: there is nothing for a remote caller to invoke because there is no pending request on its side to answer.
commandReasons.cli_bridge_host_state_publish: The CLI-bridge twin of companion_host_state_publish, publishing the same post-commit event onto CliBridgeServerState.host_state_events. Same receipt role, same already-exposed operator surface.
commandReasons.companion_host_state_publish: Broadcast receipt, not an operator action: it rejects every topic but host-state://action and republishes the event on the companion EventBus after the TypeScript authority has already committed its ledger transaction (lib/companion/desktop-write-source.ts:470). The operator surface is host_state_submit / host_state_snapshot / host_state_status, all already in KNOWN_COMMANDS.
commandReasons.companion_media_response: The renderer's response leg for GET /api/sessions/{id}/media/{hash}: it reads x-cognia-request-id / content-type / etag headers and a raw InvokeBody body (10 MB cap) and hands it to desktop_messages_bridge.resolve_media. A `tauri::ipc::Request` signature carrying a raw body has no JSON-RPC expression at all, and the operator-facing half is the HTTP route itself.
commandReasons.companion_migrate_legacy_device_grants: One-shot import carrying the renderer's soon-to-be-deleted Dexie allow-lists into the host security store, driven by the renderer at startup with the renderer's own data — not an operator action, and nothing a remote caller possesses the input for. It shares a run-once marker with SecurityStore::migrate_legacy_device_grants, which is the headless side's own path for the same import.
commandReasons.companion_worker_ack_events: Advances the worker event cursor the attached channel is draining. Cursor plumbing for a channel a remote caller does not hold.
commandReasons.companion_worker_attach_channel: Hands the renderer a Channel<T> for one worker's frames. Same channel constraint as the proxy stream family.
commandReasons.companion_worker_detach_channel: Releases the channel companion_worker_attach_channel handed out.
commandReasons.companion_worker_send_frame: Writes one frame onto the attached worker channel.
commandReasons.plugin_python_host_response: The renderer's answer to a Python plugin's reverse host_request. Same shape as the hook response above and refused for the same reason.
commandReasons.proxy_http_stream_ack: Back-pressure acknowledgement for a stream opened by proxy_http_stream_open. Meaningless without that channel.
commandReasons.proxy_http_stream_cancel: Cancels a stream opened by proxy_http_stream_open. Meaningless without that channel.
commandReasons.proxy_http_stream_open: Opens a Channel<T> the desktop proxy streams response chunks over. The channel is an IPC handle that cannot be serialized onto a socket, which is why the RPC plane has no path to it at all.
commandReasons.server_ops_events_close: Closes a stream opened by server_ops_events_open.
commandReasons.server_ops_events_open: Opens the native SSE reader for a controller operation stream and returns a Channel<T>. A remote caller reads the controller's SSE endpoint directly instead.
commandReasons.telemetry_otlp_cancel: Cancels an in-flight OTLP export this process started. There is no export on a remote caller's side to cancel.

groups.reason: The existing command depends on an interactive media lifecycle and needs a separately approved Headless-native design before exposure.

commandReasons.tts_proxy_cancel: Cancels an in-flight tts_proxy_fetch through the process-global cancellation registry that command registers into. A cancel token is meaningless without the fetch that minted it, so splitting the request lifecycle across two dispositions would make both wrong.

groups.reason: The manifest declares this command client-owned; its implementation depends on the renderer, a local window, desktop state, hardware, or an OS-local user gesture.

commandReasons.account_bind_person: Writes the local profile's person binding after a verified sign-in. The unlocked profile lives in this process; a remote caller has no unlocked session to bind.
commandReasons.account_password_rotate: Verifies the current password and rebinds the host verifier in one step. It requires the unlocked security session and the plaintext password, neither of which crosses the wire.
commandReasons.account_person: Reads the local profile's person binding out of the unlocked session.
commandReasons.account_quick_unlock_clear: Drops the account's quick-unlock keyring material on this device. The material is per device by construction, so clearing it from elsewhere would name nothing.
commandReasons.account_quick_unlock_create_verifier: Enrols a quick-unlock secret against the host-local device pepper and the unlocked security session. Neither the plaintext secret nor the pepper crosses the wire, and an enrolment is bound to the device that made it, so a remote caller has nothing to enrol against.
commandReasons.account_quick_unlock_verify: Checks a quick-unlock secret against the host verifier using the same host-local pepper. It requires the unlocked security session, which lives in this process.
commandReasons.account_unbind_person: Clears that binding. Same unlocked-session dependency as account_bind_person.
commandReasons.agent_session_api: Writes one session_api line to the sidecar's stdin through State<'_, SidecarState>, managed only by the desktop builder (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:410). Not covered by the session_* RPCs: those are brain-owned Dexie projections, while this reaches the SDK SessionStore and on-disk transcripts. Its identically shaped siblings claude_session_control / claude_feature_call / claude_feature_abort are already local-only. (The reply itself rides claude://message, which IS remotely deliverable — the blocker is the state, not the response path.)
commandReasons.agent_start: Starts the in-process agent runtime for this shell. A remote caller drives a run through the execution plane instead, which is a different question than starting this host's own runtime.
commandReasons.browser_cdp_execute: Executes CDP (Runtime.evaluate — arbitrary JS — and DOM.getDocument) against the desktop's embedded webview, resolved via app.get_webview(EMBED_LABEL), and pins the grant's origin against that webview's live URL. The Rust already answers this: `if execution_target != "local" { return Err("CDP is local-Tauri-only") }` (src-tauri/src/browser/cdp.rs:133). `browser_evaluate` is not a cover — it evaluates against a gateway browser session, a different target.
commandReasons.browser_cdp_grant: Authorization is bound to the window label holding the embedded-browser lease — `lease.assert_owner(&owner_token, invoking_window.label())` — which a remote caller has no way to present. It grants Chrome DevTools Protocol access to the desktop's embedded browser pane.
commandReasons.browser_cdp_revoke: The revoke half of browser_cdp_grant, gated on the same window-label-bound lease ownership.
commandReasons.codex_app_dispatch_conversation: Writes an owner-only transcript handoff into ~/.claude/projects, connects to Codex App's control socket under codex_home(), and if that socket is absent LAUNCHES the Codex desktop GUI through the OS opener (codex://threads/new) and polls until timeout. It returns a deep link actionable only on that desktop. The rest of the codex_app_* family is remotely exposed because those arms drive an already-running Codex App; only this one starts it.
commandReasons.codex_oauth_cancel_device_code: Cancels a device-code poll this process is running. The poll belongs to the local OAuth flow and its cancellation token never leaves the process.
commandReasons.companion_browser_access_get: Reads whether the browser-extension origin may reach this host. Local security-store read backing a desktop settings card.
commandReasons.companion_browser_access_set: Writes that decision. An OS-local trust gesture by the machine's owner, which is exactly the authority a remote caller does not hold.
commandReasons.companion_mdns_browse: Browses the local link for advertising hosts. The answer is a property of THIS machine's network segment, so running it for a remote caller would return the wrong network.
commandReasons.companion_push_notification: Fans an ids-only notification out over APNs/FCM to devices that are OFFLINE, through State<'_, CompanionServerState> — the Tauri-managed lifecycle wrapper, which cognia-server never constructs (it builds CompanionState/SharedState directly). Not covered by remote_notification_publish: that one publishes on the EventBus and so reaches devices whose socket is OPEN. They are complements. OPEN QUESTION: a headless host does install push credentials and rearm dispatchers, yet has no way to trigger a fan-out (register_push_trigger needs a tauri::Listener) and no way to set credentials. Whether headless push is meant to work is unresolved; this entry records the dependency, not a judgement that headless has no need for it.
commandReasons.companion_reachability_get: Reads the persisted reachability preference for this host.
commandReasons.companion_reachability_set: Writes it. Changing how a host can be reached is an owner gesture made at the machine.
commandReasons.companion_seed_locked_computer_use: Boot-time reconciliation of the locked-computer-use grant list from Dexie, not an operator action. Carries the same dormancy caveat as companion_set_locked_computer_use.
commandReasons.companion_set_locked_computer_use: Grants or revokes one paired device's permission to drive computer-use while the machine is locked — the same self-widening escalation risk as the terminal grant, and behind the same biometric guard. NOTE: as of this audit the allow-list it writes has no production reader; the live gate gets the answer from the security store instead. That dormancy is tracked separately and this reason must not be read as saying the ACL is load-bearing.
commandReasons.companion_set_remote_terminal: Grants or revokes one paired device's permission to open an interactive terminal on this host. Exposing it remotely would let a device that already holds a grant widen its own or hand one to another device — privilege escalation with no local gesture. Every desktop caller is wrapped in useBiometricGuard() and short-circuits for non-Tauri callers (hooks/devices/use-device-grant-actions.ts:35).
commandReasons.companion_set_ssh_files: Grants or revokes one paired device's permission to read and write the target machine over SFTP as the profile's user. ADR-0162 makes ssh.files its own grant, off by default and not implied by terminal.open, and that only holds while the switch itself is unreachable: a device that could call this would widen its own grant or hand one to another device with no local gesture. Exactly the escalation companion_set_remote_terminal is client-owned to prevent, and behind the same useBiometricGuard() in hooks/devices/use-device-grant-actions.ts.
commandReasons.companion_wake_worker: Sends a wake to a worker this process supervises.
commandReasons.connectors_ensure_server: Binds the loopback-only connectors axum listener and returns its address, starting it only if no adapter already did — the idempotent read-the-address twin of connectors_start_server (which errors on a second boot because it is the lifecycle path). Its whole purpose is to guarantee a local redirect target exists for the duration of an ADR-0134 remote-document OAuth consent round-trip, and its own doc states it always binds loopback because "an OAuth redirect target has no business being reachable off-box". A headless host has no separately started local server to address: cognia-server mounts the /connectors ingress itself, which is why the connectors_health arm reports server_running: true with bound_addr: None. Same disposition as connectors_start_server and connectors_stop_server.
commandReasons.crash_delete_submission: Deletes a local receipt from this machine's crash-report sidecar.
commandReasons.crash_refresh_submission: Re-polls the diagnostic service for one of those local receipts.
commandReasons.crash_submission_records: Reads the local submission receipts written beside those reports.
commandReasons.crash_submit_report: Uploads a crash report held in this process's on-disk sidecar. The bytes are local and the consent is an OS-local user gesture.
commandReasons.crash_withdraw_submission: Withdraws one, which the diagnostic service authorizes against the submitting machine.
commandReasons.desktop_expand_element: Expands a node of another application's OS accessibility tree; same desktop-only automation handle.
commandReasons.desktop_get_app_state: Reads another application's accessibility state AND returns a screenshot of it, redacted only when a credential window is focused. Screen capture of arbitrary applications has no remote form that the renderer-side consent overlay could bound.
commandReasons.desktop_list_apps: Reads the OS accessibility tree (AX / UIA) through State<'_, AutomationState>, which bundles the platform automation handle, permission gate, audit ring and consent broker.
commandReasons.desktop_perform_action: Drives another application's UI through the OS accessibility layer. Exposing this would hand a paired device unattended control of the whole desktop, while the HITL consent overlay that bounds the risk lives in the renderer. The remote surface deliberately carries no command that INITIATES desktop input. It carries the path to ANSWER a prompt the desktop raised (automation_consent_respond / automation_consent_pending), and the path to SUPERVISE and HALT a run that is already going (automation_settings_get / automation_kill_switch_engaged / automation_audit_snapshot, and automation_kill_switch, which is gated on the same remote-control capability as the consent reply). Watching and stopping do not hand a paired device control of the desktop, which is what this exclusion protects.
commandReasons.desktop_query_elements: Queries the OS accessibility tree of arbitrary applications through the desktop-only AutomationState.
commandReasons.desktop_zoom: Sets the zoom factor of this process's own webview.
commandReasons.dsh_runtime_facts: Reports the installed runtime under the host AppHandle data root; there is no headless equivalent of that path resolution.
commandReasons.dsh_runtime_finalize: Activates a staged runtime using a channel manifest the renderer builds.
commandReasons.dsh_runtime_install: Stages an install into the AppHandle-derived host data root using the bundled source dir.
commandReasons.dsh_runtime_remove: Takes the renderer-computed active session count to decide whether removal is safe.
commandReasons.external_agent_probe_runtime_version: Executes the agent binary on this machine to read its version. The answer describes this machine's PATH, not the caller's.
commandReasons.external_agent_sessions_read: Reads an external agent's session files off this machine's disk.
commandReasons.fleet_codex_hooks_capabilities: Spawns the local `codex` binary resolved from PATH to read which hook events its schema advertises, reporting on this machine's own Codex install (whose hooks.json lives under $HOME). Its siblings fleet_codex_hooks_install / status / uninstall are already local-only for the same reason.
commandReasons.fs_walk_workspace: Walks a workspace root on this machine's filesystem. The device-plane read for a remote caller is fs_search_content_workspace, which is root-authorized; this one is the local unbounded walk.
commandReasons.list_pi_sessions: Enumerates Pi's on-disk session records under the host's own agent directory (pi_agent_dir()); there is no headless equivalent of that path resolution. The brain answers the same question from its own runtime at cli/src/runtime/external/node-backend.ts, which is a separate implementation rather than a dispatch arm for this command.
commandReasons.ocr_http_cancel: Cancels an in-flight ocr_http_fetch through the process-global cancellation registry that command registers into; meaningless without the host-scoped fetch that minted the id.
commandReasons.ocr_http_fetch: classify_ocr_http_ip (crates/cognia-ocr/src/native.rs:253) rejects every address that is not loopback or RFC1918/ULA, so this command reaches only the host's own machine and private LAN — by design, for a self-hosted OCR endpoint. Exposing it would turn the desktop into an SSRF pivot into the user's private network with allow_private_network supplied by the caller instead of by host consent. The identical fetch/cancel pair proxy_http_request / proxy_http_cancel is already local-only.
commandReasons.open_tray_panel: Builds or reveals the transparent, undecorated, always-on-top `tray-panel` window positioned from the OS tray icon's anchor rect. There is no tray icon on a host with no desktop session.
commandReasons.pet_window_get_cursor_position: Returns the global OS cursor position in physical pixels so the local pet sprite can track the user's gaze. It reports where the user is pointing on their own screen, which is both meaningless and unwanted remotely.
commandReasons.plugin_media_add_transition: Resolves host-local source tokens before validating the transition; same barrier as plugin_media_concatenate_videos.
commandReasons.plugin_media_apply_video_effect: Resolves host-local source tokens from MediaSourceRegistry before validating the effect; same token-minting barrier as plugin_media_concatenate_videos.
commandReasons.plugin_media_concatenate_videos: Addresses clips by source_token, and tokens are minted only by video_get_info, which canonicalizes a host filesystem path and is itself local-only. A remote caller can never obtain a token, so remote invocation is impossible rather than merely unwise. Shells out to FFmpeg and writes to the host's temp dir.
commandReasons.plugin_media_export_video: Renders a timeline through FFmpeg into std::env::temp_dir()/cognia-video and returns a host-local output path that means nothing off-host. Clips arrive as source tokens only obtainable on the host.
commandReasons.plugin_python_install_uv: Downloads and installs the uv binary into this machine's plugin runtime directory.
commandReasons.plugin_workspace_repo_dir: Resolves a plugin workspace's repository directory on this machine's disk.
commandReasons.recovery_boot_get: Decides whether THIS process's WebView mounts the diagnostics shell instead of the app. Takes State<'_, RecoveryBoot> and State<'_, Arc<RecoveryController>>, both app.manage()d only inside the desktop Tauri setup() (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1699); nothing under src-tauri/src/headless/ constructs either.
commandReasons.recovery_checkpoint_record: Records one renderer initializer's health-probe outcome against the desktop-only RecoveryController. The six subsystems it accepts are renderer-side mounts.
commandReasons.recovery_heartbeat: Records renderer liveness — literally the signal that a WebView is alive. A headless server has no renderer to be alive.
commandReasons.recovery_retry: The diagnostics shell's retry gesture over desktop-only controller state; re-runs a subsystem probe or accepts keeping it disabled.
commandReasons.recovery_state_get: Returns the desktop shell's boot-health snapshot from the same desktop-only RecoveryController state.
commandReasons.reveal_tray_panel: Re-reveals the `tray-panel` window and fails outright if it no longer exists — a hard dependency on that specific desktop window.
commandReasons.selection_toolbar_copy_result: Writes to this machine's clipboard from the selection toolbar window.
commandReasons.selection_toolbar_open_permission_settin: Opens this machine's OS privacy settings pane.
commandReasons.selection_toolbar_replace: Replaces the OS-level selection in whatever application currently owns it, through the accessibility API. There is no such selection on a remote caller's side.
commandReasons.selection_toolbar_undo: Undoes that replacement, and depends on the same OS-local selection.
commandReasons.subscription_get_account_detail: Reads one provider account out of the local credential vault, including fields the list form omits. Same rationale as the rest of the subscription family (src-tauri/src/companion_api/rpc/chat.rs).
commandReasons.subscription_reauthenticate_codex_accoun: Runs the interactive Codex re-auth flow, which opens a browser on this machine.
commandReasons.subscription_refresh_codex_account: Refreshes a Codex OAuth token held in that vault.
commandReasons.subscription_replace_account_credential: Writes a provider credential into that vault.
commandReasons.terminal_close_serial: Releases a port opened by terminal_open_serial in this process. The session registry is process-local, so an id from another host names nothing.
commandReasons.terminal_detach: Sends a Detach frame to the durable terminal host and then removes this WebView's tauri::ipc::Channel<HostSeqEvent> registration. The second half is teardown of a renderer IPC channel, which has no remote analogue: a remote client detaches by closing its socket.
commandReasons.terminal_host_service: Installs, configures, or removes the durable terminal host as a per-user OS login service — on macOS by writing ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.cognia.terminal-host.plist and shelling out to launchctl (src-tauri/src/terminal_host_service.rs:230). It resolves the cognia-server binary on local disk and touches $HOME.
commandReasons.terminal_list_serial_ports: Enumerates the serial and COM devices physically attached to THIS machine. The device tree is the machine's own hardware inventory, and the ports it names exist on no other host, so there is nothing a remote caller could do with the answer except learn what is plugged in.
commandReasons.terminal_open_serial: Opens a physical device node. A serial port may be a router console, a chip programmer, or an industrial controller, and holding one open can lock out whatever else was using it. The port is one the user picked from their own machine's list, which a remote caller has no way to have done.
commandReasons.terminal_release_control: Clears the terminal session's controller lease. Reachable remotely as the ReleaseControl frame kind on /ws/terminal; filed local-only for the same subsystem-consistency reason as terminal_take_control.
commandReasons.terminal_serial_attach: Starts the read loop for a session in this process's own serial registry. The id names nothing on any other host, and the bytes it releases are emitted onto a local event topic this process owns.
commandReasons.terminal_serial_status: Reads the live state of a session in this process's own serial registry.
commandReasons.terminal_serial_write: Writes bytes to an attached device. This is the destructive direction: a stray byte to a programmer or a controller can change firmware or actuate something. Local and user-driven by construction.
commandReasons.terminal_take_control: Claims the terminal session's controller lease for the calling connection. Remote clients reach the same capability over the /ws/terminal route, which relays the TakeControl frame kind (companion_api/ws_terminal.rs:228, gated on the terminal.open capability) — so the operator is not blocked. This command is filed with the rest of its subsystem: terminal_write, terminal_resize, terminal_spawn and terminal_set_flow_control all map to frame kinds the same socket relays and are all local-only, and one subsystem should not carry two conventions.
commandReasons.toggle_tray_panel: Shows or hides the named `tray-panel` desktop window depending on its current visibility.
commandReasons.tray_panel_get_config: Reads the tray quick-panel configuration from <cognia-home>/tray-panel.json. The dependency is semantic rather than structural: the setting governs what a click on the OS tray icon does and how large the popover opens, neither of which exists without a tray.
commandReasons.tray_panel_resize: Folds a renderer-measured content size back into the `tray-panel` window's frame; both the measurement and the window are desktop-only.
commandReasons.tray_panel_set_left_click: Writes the OS tray icon's left-click behaviour to <cognia-home>/tray-panel.json. Same semantic dependency as tray_panel_get_config.
commandReasons.tray_run_native_action: Gated #[cfg(desktop)] and returns an error otherwise. Shows or hides the `main` window, or emits tray://* events that only the local renderer implements — those channels are deliberately absent from the remotely deliverable event catalog.
commandReasons.usage_dock_reveal: First-paint reveal, and the one dock command that is not merely desktop-shaped: it resolves the CALLING window and errors unless that window is the dock itself, so there is no caller outside the dock window for it to have.
commandReasons.wake_paired_host: Sends a wake-on-LAN magic frame onto this machine's local segment. Like companion_mdns_browse, the segment is the point: relaying it would wake nothing.
commandReasons.workflow_wait_event_persist: Inserts the wait-event row an event_wait waitpoint consumes — machine-to-machine plumbing driven by the renderer orchestrator, not an operator action.
commandReasons.workflow_wait_event_prune: Renderer-driven garbage collection of its own mirror (DELETE FROM workflow_wait_event WHERE expires_at <= ?), invoked from lib/db/workflow-waitpoints.ts:315.
commandReasons.workflow_waitpoint_create: Write-through of a renderer-authored Dexie record into its host SQLite mirror (lib/db/workflow-waitpoints.ts:163 dual-writes after the Dexie add). The renderer store is the author of every waitpoint; the native row exists to arbitrate a decide race. Same role as workflow_persist_run_state.
commandReasons.workflow_waitpoint_get: The renderer's read-back leg of the same mirror sync, used to probe before and after a decide (lib/db/workflow-waitpoints.ts:174).

groups.reason: Mints a code whose whole content is an address on the Host's own loopback interface. The browser plane is plaintext `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` by construction — that is the one origin a tab trusts without a certificate — so a code handed to a remote caller names a listener on the wrong machine. These commands are therefore local by the shape of what they return, not by a renderer dependency.

commandReasons.companion_create_browser_enrollment: Returns `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:{port}` built from `state.browser_port()`, the live bound port of this process's plaintext loopback listener (companion_api/mod.rs:449 spawns it; `CompanionServerState::browser_port` is `None` when it did not bind, which is why the command refuses rather than minting a code that cannot connect). A remote caller redeeming that code would be pointed at its own loopback, not the Host's. Unlike `companion_create_worker_enrollment` — whose HTTPS/tunnel baseUrl is reachable from anywhere and which is therefore covered by the `fleet_worker_enrollment_create` RPC arm — there is no remotely-meaningful form of this code, so there is nothing for a Headless arm to return. The extension that spends it runs in a browser on the Host's own machine and reaches it over that same loopback; the operator copies the code from Settings → Companion into the extension's connection screen.
